rules.statement: Do not bake deployment or tier configuration such as OAuth client ids or redirect URIs into a frontend bundle at build time (env vars, .env files); discover it at runtime from the host's bootstrap configuration endpoint.
rules.why: The platform's 'one bundle, every tier' invariant requires one build artifact to run in every tier; the client id is a deployment coordinate discovered at boot.
rules.check: Look for client ids, issuer URLs or other tier coordinates read from import.meta.env, process.env or .env files, or hard-coded in SPA source, instead of loaded from the runtime bootstrap config.

rules.statement: Interactive OAuth/OIDC client code and developer tooling must offer only the authorization-code flow with PKCE using S256; do not make the implicit, hybrid front-channel-token or resource-owner-password flows, or the `plain` PKCE method, selectable.
rules.why: The security-practice default exposes only the recommended flow; tooling that can emit implicit or hybrid requests would make insecure patterns look normal.
rules.check: Look for response_type values other than `code`, grant_type=password or implicit, code_challenge_method=plain, or UI options that let users pick these flows.

rules.statement: OIDC authorization requests built by client code must include a `nonce` and check it against the ID token, alongside `state` and PKCE.
rules.why: The nonce ties the ID token to the request so it cannot be replayed.
rules.check: Look for authorize URL builders or OIDC sign-in flows that send the openid scope without generating a nonce, or that never compare the ID token's nonce claim with the stored value.

rules.statement: Put protocol orchestration and security-audit logic in UI-free modules that have their own unit tests, and keep it out of UI components.
rules.why: Keeping flow and audit logic out of the UI makes it unit-testable and lets it be built from shared primitives.
rules.check: Look for OAuth flow steps, token handling or metadata-audit rules written inside React components or views with no matching UI-free module and unit tests.
